records.deidentified_narrative: -on [date] at about 0425 hours, i, cpl. p. krekel #286, was contacted by on-duty cpl. j. kirchner, in regards to a fatality motor vehicle accident involving a pedestrian, in about the 2100 block of n ih35 e, desoto, dallas county, tx. i, along with ofc. gonzalez #333, responded and arrived to the crash scene at about 0543 hours. upon arrival, i was briefed by cpl. kirchner about the crash. i observed a black male wearing a red hoodie and red sweat pants, with clothes cut off his body, exposing his back and buttocks. he was lying in the safety divider for exit 416 to wintergreen on ih 35e, in front of global industrial distribution (2119 n ih35e sr, desoto). there was a wig lying nearby, that i was advised came from the male. the male was clearly deceased, and was pronounced by medics at about 0410hours. the male had marks consistent with being struck by a vehicle. the body was positioned with the head pointing west, slightly northwest. i observed blood pooling around the head of the body. i conducted a walkthrough of the scene at this point. there was no identification on or near the decedent, so he was no able to be positively identified at the scene. he was a black male, about 58 thin build, with slight facial hair, and short haircut style, but not faded or bald. from the body, i observed three short skip skids, that go about 50 feet north from the body, to a flip flop lying in the safety zone. going north from the flip flop, i observed about a 200 foot long straight skid. in that skid path, there was debris from a headlight. on the west side of the exit ramp, there was a piece of black bumper. the bumper piece was looked over, and red fibers matching the color of the decedents clothing, was observed. all pieces leading up to the decedent were collected. one piece that was collected, has a marking of 2f4v-0, which when googled, comes back as a toyota part number 52145-33050. tis part number belongs to a front bumper bracket for a 2007-2012 lexus [identifier]. this part also had red fibers stuck to it. i compared the item collected to a similar vehicle, the toyota avalon, and the pieces do not look similar, leading me to believe the part comes from a lexus [identifier]. after all photographs were taken, the medical examiner was notified. she arrived and took custody of the decedent. she provided their report number (ifs-23-13232). she advised she would reach out to me, once a positive identification of the decedent was made. i added the offense of accident involving death, to this report, due to the victim being struck by a car, and the driver failing provide the victim reasonable assistance, including transporting or making arrangements [medical facility] for medical treatment if it is apparent that treatment is necessary, as well as, the suspect, being involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of a person or damage to a vehicle to the extent that it cannot be normally and safely driven, failed to immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the accident to the local police department (desoto police) if the accident occurred in a municipality. since it appears the decedent was maybe coming from [roadway], i contacted lancaster pd to see if they had any calls about him, but phyllis in dispatch advised they did not have any welfare checks in the area or missing persons reports from last night. a check of the bumper piece collected, showed the following imprint pp40/p-td2c tsop. i was unable to find anything of merit, so i reached out to south toyota parts department in dallas for their assistance, and went to their location with the pieces. the vehicle parts were able to be narrowed down further, to a 2007-2009 lexus [identifier]. --on [date] at about 1433 hours, i, cpl. p. krekel #286, received notification from the medical examiner's office, that there was a positive identification on the victim. he was identified as samuel stroggins (b/m dob [date]). -on [date] at about 0645 hours, i ran samuel stroggins on ncic to get information on stroggins, and a missing person with disability hit came up for him. he was listed as missing on [date] under dallas [case id] # [phone]. i reached out to dallas missing person unit, and spoke with detective perez, dpd #10706. i updated him on his missing person case. he was able to provide me with their [case id], along with a next of kin (melonie moton [phone]). the report states that scroggins is diagnosed with bi-polar disorder and schizophrenia, and that he had been acting extremely erratic due to the progression of his mental illness. at about 1015hours, i was able to make contact with melonie, and conducted a death notification with her. i then updated the medical examiner's office with the information i had. -on [date], i went to swifs in dallas with property tech hamilton to drop off the vehicle pieces that had red fibers in them, in order for swifs to do a fiber comparison to the victim's clothing. at this time, i still have no viable leads. i have reviewed several tips that have come in, but none panned out.

records.public_safe_text: -on [date] at about 0425 hours, i, cpl. p. krekel #286, was contacted by on-duty cpl. j. kirchner, in regards to a fatality motor vehicle accident involving a pedestrian, in about the 2100 block of n ih35 e, desoto, dallas county, tx. i, along with ofc. gonzalez #333, responded and arrived to the crash scene at about 0543 hours. upon arrival, i was briefed by cpl. kirchner about the crash. i observed a black male wearing a red hoodie and red sweat pants, with clothes cut off his body, exposing his back and buttocks. he was lying in the safety divider for exit 416 to wintergreen on ih 35e, in front of global industrial distribution (2119 n ih35e sr, desoto). there was a wig lying nearby, that i was advised came from the male. the male was clearly deceased, and was pronounced by medics at about 0410hours. the male had marks consistent with being struck by a vehicle. the body was positioned with the head pointing west, slightly northwest. i observed blood pooling around the head of the body. i conducted a walkthrough of the scene at this point. there was no identification on or near the decedent, so he was no able to be positively identified at the scene. he was a black male, about 58 thin build, with slight facial hair, and short haircut style, but not faded or bald. from the body, i observed three short skip skids, that go about 50 feet north from the body, to a flip flop lying in the safety zone. going north from the flip flop, i observed about a 200 foot long straight skid. in that skid path, there was debris from a headlight. on the west side of the exit ramp, there was a piece of black bumper. the bumper piece was looked over, and red fibers matching the color of the decedents clothing, was observed. all pieces leading up to the decedent were collected. one piece that was collected, has a marking of 2f4v-0, which when googled, comes back as a toyota part number 52145-33050. tis part number belongs to a front bumper bracket for a 2007-2012 lexus [identifier]. this part also had red fibers stuck to it. i compared the item collected to a similar vehicle, the toyota avalon, and the pieces do not look similar, leading me to believe the part comes from a lexus [identifier]. after all photographs were taken, the medical examiner was notified. she arrived and took custody of the decedent. she provided their report number (ifs-23-13232). she advised she would reach out to me, once a positive identification of the decedent was made. i added the offense of accident involving death, to this report, due to the victim being struck by a car, and the driver failing provide the victim reasonable assistance, including transporting or making arrangements [medical facility] for medical treatment if it is apparent that treatment is necessary, as well as, the suspect, being involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of a person or damage to a vehicle to the extent that it cannot be normally and safely driven, failed to immediately by the quickest means of communication give notice of the accident to the local police department (desoto police) if the accident occurred in a municipality. since it appears the decedent was maybe coming from [roadway], i contacted lancaster pd to see if they had any calls about him, but phyllis in dispatch advised they did not have any welfare checks in the area or missing persons reports from last night. a check of the bumper piece collected, showed the following imprint pp40/p-td2c tsop. i was unable to find anything of merit, so i reached out to south toyota parts department in dallas for their assistance, and went to their location with the pieces. the vehicle parts were able to be narrowed down further, to a 2007-2009 lexus [identifier]. --on [date] at about 1433 hours, i, cpl. p. krekel #286, received notification from the medical examiner's office, that there was a positive identification on the victim. he was identified as samuel stroggins (b/m dob [date]). -on [date] at about 0645 hours, i ran samuel stroggins on ncic to get information on stroggins, and a missing person with disability hit came up for him. he was listed as missing on [date] under dallas [case id] # [phone]. i reached out to dallas missing person unit, and spoke with detective perez, dpd #10706. i updated him on his missing person case. he was able to provide me with their [case id], along with a next of kin (melonie moton [phone]). the report states that scroggins is diagnosed with bi-polar disorder and schizophrenia, and that he had been acting extremely erratic due to the progression of his mental illness. at about 1015hours, i was able to make contact with melonie, and conducted a death notification with her. i then updated the medical examiner's office with the information i had. -on [date], i went to swifs in dallas with property tech hamilton to drop off the vehicle pieces that had red fibers in them, in order for swifs to do a fiber comparison to the victim's clothing. at this time, i still have no viable leads. i have reviewed several tips that have come in, but none panned out.

records.deidentified_narrative: while on patrol police responded to a major accident involving a vehicle and a pedestrian at the listed location. upon arrival officer trevino # 0593 and officer lang # 0416 were managing the scene. the officers advised me that there were (2) people who witnessed the incident. this incident occurred on private property. the unit 1 driver stated that he drove next to the gas pumps to park his vehicle so as to go get something to drink inside of the incident location. the unit 1 driver added that as he was driving into the gas pump spot another unknown vehicle pulled into the same gas pump spot with the intention of pumping gas into their vehicle. the unit 1 driver stated that he wanted [roadway] of the other unknown vehicle who drove in front of unit 1. the unknown vehicle wanted to get in the same gas pump location that the unit 1 driver initially had. unit 1 stated that he moved his vehicle (the unit 1 driver reversed his vehicle and drove backwards) to avoid any issues. the unit 1 driver stated that he drove unit 1 in reverse and backed up without looking at unit 1's back up camera or the rear view mirror or the rear side view mirrors and unit 1 struck unit 2 with the back end of unit 1. the unit 1 driver stated that he felt the rear tires of his vehicle raise up as he struck/ran over unit 2. unit 1 also stated that after hitting/running over unit 2 with his vehicle that witnesses started screaming and yelling at the unit 1 driver. the unit 1 driver said that he got scared due to the yelling and commotion, so the unit 1 driver then drove the vehicle forward running over unit 2 once more with his rear tires. unit 2 suffered multiple severe physical injuries due to this incident. [medical facility] (bamc) by ambulance. unit 2 had a fractured skull and a broken left arm. unit 2 succumbed to his [medical facility] on [date]. the unit 1 driver had no observed or reported physical injuries. there was active video surveillance that recorded this incident. i observed the recorded surveillance video of the motor vehicle accident between unit 1 and unit 2. the unit 1 driver was given a traffic citation for not have having a valid drivers license. the unit 1 driver had a friend arrive on location with a valid driver's license, and drove unit 1 away to an unknown location. unit 2's property was released to his family after unit 2's family member signed a completed release of property form (a completed and signed duplicate release of property form was routed to the south substation's supervisors). there were no observations of intoxication from the unit 1 driver. supervisor buso # 3263 made the location and was briefed on the incident. csi rackley # 9412 processes the scene. traffic investigation unit (tid) detective pawelek #2131 processed the incident location.
